judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures hold, and problem 9 is worse than described. Its stem asks for three things - 'Estimate the difference to the nearest hundred', 'use your estimate to explain, in one sentence, why 655 stickers cannot be right', and 'work 703 - 158 correctly' - and verify.json id 9 is a single eval for 545. So the required explanation is unverified AND unflagged, and the required estimate (700 - 200 = 500) has no entry either, even though `estimate` is the very type used ten times elsewhere in this file. On problems 5 and 6 the judge is exact: 5(c) says 'Is your exact answer close to your estimate? Write yes or no' and id 5 carries only the estimate 400 and the exact 409; 6(b) says 'Does the check give back 623 pages?' and id 6 carries only 727 and 448. verify.json has no manual entry anywhere, so final_response.md's claim - 'Zero entries are manual - the reasonableness judgments are all anchored to a checkable number, so nothing was left unverifiable' - is a false trust statement about the sheet's own problem 9. One item the judge did not list: problem 3 also asks the student to 'write one sentence saying how many apples were in the crate at the start' and only the sum 340 is checked.

strengths_to_preserve: The three-tool directions box (estimate, is-it-reasonable, check-by-adding) is followed by a fully worked model using the same crayon numbers - 506 rounds to 500, 291 to 300, estimate 200, exact 215, check 215 + 291 = 506 - so the student sees the entire cycle once before problem 1. That worked pattern is exactly what the representations-applications mode needs.

The key distinguishes estimates from exact values in its notation and its grading advice: solution 1 writes 400 - 200 = 200, then adds 'the exact difference is 225 books, so an estimate of 200 books is a good one. Accept the estimate only when both numbers were rounded'. That gives a grader a rule for a class of answers that are not simply right or wrong.

Problem 10 (900 - 348 - 275 rounded to hundreds) extends the estimate type to a three-operand expression and the `estimate` check rounds each operand independently, so the hardest item on the sheet is still inside the gate rather than being downgraded to manual.

root_causes.description: The coverage gate is defined per problem id, not per printed response. verify.py fails only when some id in 1..problem_count has no entry at all, so a problem that prints several required responses is fully satisfied by one scalar check, and both the gate log and the delivery message then describe the sheet as completely verified.
evidence: worksheet problem 9 prints three required responses (estimate, one-sentence explanation, exact difference) and verify.json id 9 is one eval for 545.
worksheet problem 5 has parts (a), (b) and (c); id 5 has two entries and no check for the (c) yes/no judgment.
worksheet problem 6 has parts (a) and (b) where (b) asks 'Does the check give back 623 pages?'; id 6 has two entries, both numeric.
worksheet problem 3 asks for the sum and a sentence; id 3 is one eval for 340.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to reframe error-analysis items 'via the ordinary types' and, a few lines later, to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Nothing states that an item doing both needs both entries, and no gate enforces it, so the explanation slot is dropped and the sheet reports zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet problem 9 requires a written reasonableness explanation and verify.json declares no manual entry anywhere in the file.
final_response.md: 'Nothing is flagged for manual review' and 'Zero entries are manual', on a sheet that prints 'explain, in one sentence'.

root_causes.description: Yes/no reasonableness judgments are objectively checkable but have no type to carry them, so an author who wants full coverage has to either invent an encoding or leave the slot out. Both problems 5(c) and 6(b) took the second route.
evidence: worksheet 5(c): 'Is your exact answer close to your estimate? Write yes or no.' - no entry in verify.json covers it.
worksheet 6(b): 'Does the check give back 623 pages?' - no entry covers it.
SKILL.md's type table offers no boolean/judgment type; the nearest, `compare` with a relation, does not express 'is this within a tolerance of the estimate'.

root_causes.description: final_response.md is composed by hand rather than derived from verify.json and gate_log.txt, so its factual claims about verification coverage, manual items and page counts drift from the artifacts they describe.
evidence: final_response.md asserts 'All 13 verify entries ... are machine-checked' and 'Zero entries are manual' while worksheet problem 9 prints an explanation slot.

improvements.title: Make verification coverage per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py's coverage gate currently passes as soon as every id in 1..problem_count carries one entry (scripts/verify.py, the `missing = [i for i in range(1, problem_count + 1) if i not in ids]` check). Replace that with a slot-level contract: add a build gate that counts the response slots a problem actually prints (each \ansline/\answerline/\ansblank, each \underline{} write-on rule in a stem, each lettered part (a)/(b)/(c), each row of a fill-in table or partially blank sequence) and fails the build unless that id declares at least as many verify entries. Add the matching rule to SKILL.md's JSON-format paragraph, which today only says 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'. Problem 9 alone prints three required responses against one check; problems 3, 5 and 6 each print one more response than they declare.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_answer_slots.py plus a fixture pair under tests/fixtures/: a worksheet .tex whose problem 1 prints two response slots (an inline \underline{} line inside the stem and \problem's automatic answer blank) and a verify.json carrying a single scalar entry for id 1. The gate must exit 1 naming 'problem 1 prints 2 response slots but declares 1 check'. Today build.sh runs that fixture green, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the dominant hard-failure class in this shard: a worksheet can no longer print several required responses per problem while reporting itself fully verified.
improvements.risk: Slot counting is a heuristic over LaTeX and prose, so it will over-count on stems that use \underline for emphasis. Keep it a fail-with-named-slot gate (never a silent skip) and allow an explicit per-problem "slots" override in the verify JSON so a genuine one-slot problem can declare that rather than being blocked.

improvements.title: Require a paired manual entry for every explain / name-the-error / mark-it response
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md carries two rules that pull in opposite directions: the reframing paragraph says error analysis should be encoded 'via the ordinary types - the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right', while the paragraph eight lines later says to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Authors resolve that by encoding only the numeric correction and dropping the explanation slot. Rewrite the reframing paragraph to state the pairing explicitly: an error-analysis or model-completion item that ALSO prints an explain / name-the-error / circle / cross-out / draw / label slot needs BOTH the typed check for the correction AND a manual entry for that slot under the same id (the curr-088 and curr-100 verify files in this same shard are the worked pattern). Back it with the slot gate so the rule is mechanical, not advisory. Problem 9's 'explain in one sentence why 655 stickers cannot be right' is the unflagged open response here, and problem 3's closing sentence is a second.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_answer_slots.py with a fixture whose problem stem contains an imperative open-response verb ('Explain in one sentence', 'Circle', 'Draw', 'Label', 'Cross out', 'Which measurement did ... actually find?') and whose verify.json entry for that id is a bare eval. The gate must exit 1 demanding a paired {"type": "manual"} entry. The same fixture passes once the manual entry is added. Today it passes in both states, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The build's manual-item count becomes trustworthy: exit 2 and the 'flagged manual-review items' banner appear whenever a sheet asks a child to explain, mark or draw something, instead of the build reporting all-green on unreviewed reasoning.
improvements.risk: More sheets exit 2 rather than 0, which looks like a regression on dashboards that treat exit 0 as success. That is the intended trust signal; document it in the build-driver section of SKILL.md so exit 2 is not read as a failure.

improvements.title: Add a checkable type for yes/no reasonableness and check-by-adding judgments
improvements.proposed_change: Add a `judgment` check to scripts/verify.py: "claim" as an expression or relation the verifier evaluates (e.g. "abs(409 - 400) <= 50" for 'is the exact answer close to the estimate', or "552 + 175 == 623" for 'does the check give back the start') with "expected": true|false. The verifier decides the truth value itself, so the yes/no the student writes is genuinely gated instead of being dropped or hand-waved into an adjacent numeric entry. Note the type in SKILL.md's table and in the reframing paragraph beside estimation and ordering.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_branches.py add judgment cases: "552 + 175 == 623" with expected false PASSES (the check does not give back 623) and with expected true FAILS; "abs(409 - 400) <= 50" with expected true PASSES. All three are schema errors today (exit 1, unknown type), so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The reasonableness facet - the thing this worksheet is about - becomes verifiable rather than being represented only by the numbers on either side of the judgment.
improvements.risk: A boolean claim can be written to be trivially true. Require the claim to reference the same numbers as the problem's other entries, and reject a claim with no free numeric content, so the type cannot be used as a rubber stamp.

case_summary: The estimation and checking mathematics is correct throughout - all ten independently recomputed results agree with the key, and the rounding rule (look at the tens digit for hundreds) is taught, practised and trapped consistently. The sheet fails on verification honesty rather than on content. Problem 9 asks for an estimate, a written explanation and an exact difference and declares one check for the last of the three; problems 5(c) and 6(b) print objective yes/no judgments no entry covers; problem 3's closing sentence is likewise uncovered. Because verify.json declares no manual entry at all, the build reports all-green and the delivery message states outright that nothing was left unverifiable, which is not true of the sheet's own problem 9.
